## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless blend keeping the death verdict in registers can sustain near-ceiling bandwidth by eliminating branchy respawn overhead.

## Layout & approach
The AoS Particle at 68 B/p offers 32 hot bytes (47%) to loop1 — age+pos+seed+vel — and 28 (41%) to loop2, with no intermediate storage so the verdict stays in registers. Integration is delegated to an AOT `halide_b2` call; death uses csel-based blend. The 53% dead weight per cache line means even perfect streaming wastes half the bandwidth; the working set spills L1d at N≈963 and L2 at N≈61680, but the identity ordering's sequential access should stay prefetch-friendly.

## Cache saturation
Cost is remarkably flat: ~4.7–4.9 ns/p in L1d (N≤960), a modest bump to ~5.1–5.3 at N=10000–25000 in L2, then settling to ~4.6–4.9 in DRAM (N≥62000). No sharp knee at either spill — the L1d→L2 transition is invisible and L2→DRAM slightly improves, because streaming stays prefetch-friendly and the 146-insn body amortizes overhead. The L2 bump at N=10000–25000 reflects scalar FP and byte-scatter overhead, not memory latency.

## Bandwidth
Achieved ~14.4 GB/s (48% of the 29.9 ceiling) at q=0.01, matching the 47% hot fraction — compute-bound by the 146-insn scalar loop (compute 68–76% at N≤1M), not memory-limited, though AoS dead weight caps useful bandwidth. The 2.274 ns/p floor frames the gap: 4.7 ns/p is ~2.1x irreducible memory time. At q=0.5, BW drops to ~12.5 GB/s (42%) as backend_stall climbs to 43.2% at N=10M — respawn scatter shifts the bottleneck toward memory. Versus baseline: 0.65x at q=0.01 improving to 0.40x at q=0.5; versus winner: 1.30x slower at q=0.01 (N=380) where autovec's SIMD dominates, but 1.0x at q≥0.1.

## Assembly
Codegen is almost entirely scalar: 2 vector insns across 353, with integration delegated to `bl _halide_b2`. Loop1 runs ~146 insns/iter at stride 68B with scalar FP (`fmul`, `fadd`, `fsub`, `fcvtzs`) and 12 `csel` for the branchless death blend. The render path uses 16 `strb` byte-granular scatter stores with `ldrb`/`uqadd`/`csel` saturation clamping — these byte writes cannot stream and cap bandwidth. The 14 branches per iter are render bounds checks; branch_flush stays modest (3.9–7.8%). No component-wise vectorization explains why autovec wins at q=0.01: it SIMDs across particles where this code cannot.

## Verdict
Partially holds — the branchless blend keeps branch_flush under 8% and wins at q≥0.1 (1.0x winner, 0.40–0.57x baseline), but at q=0.01 it loses to autovec (1.30x winner at N=380, 1.09x at N=10M) because scalar FP and byte-granular scatter cannot match SIMD streaming. 48% of ceiling matching 47% hot confirms: the blend eliminates branch overhead but not layout waste.
